title: Profound Medical Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: – Operating expenses decline 16%, helping drive a 39% improvement in net loss – – Approximately $3.1 million of TULSA revenue…...
body_text: Profound Medical Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results August 06, 2026 4:12pm EDT Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio 10-Q HTML XBRL Zip – Operating expenses decline 16%, helping drive a 39% improvement in net loss – – Approximately $3.1 million of TULSA revenue recognition shifts into early Q3 due to shipment timing – – Strong clinical, commercial and reimbursement momentum continues – – Company reiterates full-year 2026 revenue guidance – – Announces first employer owned health plans to list the TULSA Procedure™ as a covered service – TORONTO, Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Profound Medical Corp. (NASDAQ:PROF; TSX:PRN) (“Profound” or the “Company”), a commercial-stage medical device company that develops and markets innovative interventional MRI (“iMRI”) procedures, today announced financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Unless specified otherwise, all amounts in this press release are expressed in U.S. dollars and are presented in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (U.S. GAAP). “Commercial momentum continued to accelerate during the second quarter," said Arun Menawat, Profound's CEO and Chairman. “We received over $7.0 million in new purchase orders, a new quarterly record. Approximately $2.5 million of those orders were recognized as revenue during the quarter, while approximately $3.1 million was shipped in July and will be recognized in the third quarter. The shipment timing reflected a temporary logistics issue—not customer demand—and, absent the timing difference, second quarter revenue would have increased approximately 153% year-over-year. The logistics issue has since been resolved. Beyond top-line growth, our business model continued to demonstrate meaningful operating leverage. Gross margin remained above our long-term target of 70%, operating expenses declined 16%, and net loss improved by 39% year-over-year. Momentum has continued into the third quarter, including another monthly record for new order activity in July and exceptional physician engagement at SRS2026 that generated more than 160 qualified commercial opportunities over just four days. Based on continued payer coverage expansion, growing clinical validation, and a strengthening sales pipeline, we believe we are now in the strongest commercial position in the Company's history. Based on this momentum and our improved visibility into the second half of the year, we are reiterating the $25.0 million bar we previously set for 2026 total revenue." Business Highlights Clinical Momentum The post-market CAPTAIN Level 1 randomized clinical data continued to demonstrate statistically significant advantages of the TULSA Procedure™ over robotic radical prostatectomy, with new penile length preservation data presented in July 2026 . Physician awareness of, and engagement with, the TULSA Procedure continued to expand through presentations at the 2026 meetings of the Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR), the American Urological Association (AUA), and the Society of Robotic Surgery (SRS). Reimbursement Expansion Payer coverage expanded by approximately 18.3 million covered lives during the second quarter, substantially broadening patient access to the TULSA Procedure. Most of the newly covered lives came through state Medicaid and managed Medicaid (Ambetter) programs. Today, Profound is pleased to announce that the Johns Hopkins Employee Health Plan and the Prime Healthcare Employee Health Plan, covering more than 50,000 and 55,000 employees, medical staff and family members, respectively, have become the first employer owned health plans to list the TULSA Procedure as a covered service. Commercial Execution & Adoption Profound’s TULSA-PRO® installed base increased to 84 at the end of Q2-2026. Profound estimates that the current aggregate total dollar value of its qualified sales pipeline (defined as within one of the “Verify, Negotiate and Contracting” stages) for TULSA-PRO and Sonalleve® is approximately $70.0 million.* Continuing Innovation Profound also launched an initiative to explore the potential of integrating PSMA PET molecular imaging technologies with the TULSA Procedure to support intention-to-treat decisions and patient monitoring. * There can be no assurance given with respect to the extent and/or timing of the Company’s qualified sales pipeline resulting in recognized revenue. Q2-2026 Clinical Utilization Trends Physicians continued to utilize the TULSA Procedure’s customizable prostate tissue ablation capabilities in the second quarter of 2026: Prostate Condition Ablation of malignant prostate tissue Ablation of malignant and benign enlarged prostate tissue Ablation of recurrent malignant prostate tissue Ablation of benign enlarged prostate tissue 71% (12% GG1, 58% GG2, 21% GG3, 9% GG4&5) 14% 11% 4% Regional Ablation Whole-gland Sub-total but more than half the gland Hemi-ablation Focal therapy 43% 24% 21% 12% Prostate Size < 20 cc 20-40 cc 40-60 cc 60-100 cc > 100 cc 8% 39% 31% 17% 5% TULSA INDEX20 Introduced by the Company in the first quarter of 2026, the following supplemental ‘same-store’ TULSA Procedure volume analysis is designed to track a fixed cohort (i.e. without any changes or substitutions) of 20 active commercial TULSA-PRO sites over time. The TULSA INDEX20 includes a representative variety of providers, including teaching hospitals and private-pay practices, all of which have been performing TULSA Procedures for at least 12 months. Geographically, 80% of the index sites are in the U.S. and 20% are international. TULSA INDEX20 Q2-2025 Q3-2025 Q4-2025 Q1-2026 Q2-2026 # TULSA Sites 20 20 20 20 20 Average Procedures/Quarter 8.2 8.6 10.3 11.3 10.0 Average Procedures Annualized 32.8 34.4 41.2 45.2 40.0 Quarter-Over-Quarter Sequential Growth 15% 5% 20% 10% (12%) H1-2026 Over H1-2025 Growth 39% Quarterly Year-Over-Year Growth 22% Summary Second Quarter 2026 Results For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Profound recorded total revenue of approximately $2.5 million, up 12% year-over-year, including $1.6 million of recurring non-capital revenue from single-use devices and services associated with extended warranties, and $871,000 from capital equipment sales. Approximately $3.1 million of TULSA product shipments originally anticipated in the final week of June were completed in July. The timing affected only the period of revenue recognition and did not reflect any change in customer demand or order activity. Excluding this shipment timing, second quarter revenue would have been approximately $5.6 million, representing 153% year-over-year growth. Gross margin expanded to 78% in Q2-2026 from 73% in the prior-year period, reflecting a favorable product mix, including multiple capital system sales that were previously under operating leases to customers. Operating expenses declined 16% year over year to approximately $13.0 million, primarily reflecting lower personnel, commercial, travel, insurance and CAPTAIN clinical trial costs following completion of enrollment. These reductions were partially offset by higher R&D investments focused on product cost reduction, quality improvements and manufacturing efficiencies. Second quarter 2026 net loss was approximately $9.5 million, or $0.26 per common share, a 39% improvement from a net loss of approximately $15.7 million, or $0.52 per common share, in the three months ended June 30, 2025. Liquidity and Outstanding Share Capital As at June 30, 2026, Profound had cash of approximately $38.3 million. As at August 6, 2026, Profound had 36,532,594 common shares issued and outstanding. For complete financial results, please see Profound’s filings, which will be made available under Profound’s profile at www.sedarplus.com , www.sec.gov and on Profound’s website under “SEC & SEDAR+ Filings.” Full Year 2026 Financial Outlook Based on record order activity, continued expansion of its commercial pipeline and improved visibility into second-half shipments, Profound continues to project total revenue for full-year 2026 to be approximately $25.0 million, which represents 56% growth compared to its prior year revenue. The Company also continues to expect full year 2026 gross margin to be 70% or higher. Conference Call Details Profound is pleased to invite all interested parties to participate in a conference call today at 4:30 pm ET during which time the results will be discussed. To participate in the conference call by telephone, please pre-register via this link to receive the dial-in number and your unique PIN. The call will also be broadcast live and archived on Profound's website in the Investors section here . About Profound Medical Corp. Profound is a commercial-stage medical device company and an innovator in interventional MRI (iMRI) procedures. The company’s flagship platform, TULSA-PRO® , enables MRI-guided, incision-free prostate ablation. Physicians use the TULSA Procedure™ to see, ablate, and confirm therapy in real time, supporting personalized treatment strategies across the continuum of prostate care—from whole-gland to subtotal, hemi, multifocal, and focal treatment. This approach enables individualized care using prostate tissue ablation, while minimizing the potential of the side effects that are typically associated with surgery or radiation, such as urinary incontinence and/or erectile dysfunction. Profound also commercializes Sonalleve® , an MRI-guided therapy that provides a non-surgical treatment option for pain palliation of bone metastases, desmoid tumors, and osteoid osteoma, as well as for common gynecologic conditions including uterine fibroids and adenomyosis. Sonalleve delivers targeted therapy with no incisions, no blood loss during the procedure, no overnight hospital stay, and faster recovery — and, in gynecologic applications, enables uterine-sparing treatment that may help preserve fertility. Profound is also exploring additional clinical applications for Sonalleve, including non-invasive ablation of abdominal cancers and hyperthermia-based cancer therapies. Profound Medical’s technologies are approved across major global markets. TULSA-PRO is cleared by the FDA in the United States for transurethral ultrasound ablation (TULSA) of prostate tissue. In addition, TULSA-PRO is cleared for use in various jurisdictions including Europe, Canada, Saudi Arabia, India, Australia/New Zealand, and the UAE. Sonalleve is approved by the FDA as HDE in the United States for the treatment of osteoid osteomas in the extremities. Sonalleve is also cleared or approved in the Europe, Canada, China, and Saudi Arabia. Through real-time MRI guidance and data-driven innovation, Profound is advancing the future of MRI-guided therapy — expanding access to precise, personalized, and incision-free treatment options worldwide. title: Life of a product manager at Belvo
summary: What it's like to be a product manager at Belvo: cross-team collaboration, autonomy, and building fintech products across Brazil and Mexico.
body_text: Ask a product manager at most companies what their week looks like, and you'll hear about roadmaps and sprint planning. Ask a product manager at Belvo, and you'll get a different answer: sales calls, regulatory filings, a cost calculation for a client renewal, and a strategy session with the CEO, sometimes all in the same day. Belvo is Latin America's leading open finance platform, operating across Brazil and Mexico. Our product covers Open Finance and employment data, and payments, plus the AI layer that sits on top , for both Mexico and Brazil. Because the business is so horizontal, being a PM here means owning a slice of nearly everything: sales, customer success, engineering, and regulation included. We talked to three of our product managers, Kevin Nakabashi, Senior Product Manager in Brazil, Andrés Alanís, Senior Product Manager in Mexico, and Daniel Bañuelos, Group Product Manager focused on Payments in Mexico, about what the role actually looks like. AN UNUSUAL REPORTING LINE At most companies, product sits several layers removed from the CEO. At Belvo, product and engineering report directly to Uri Tintoré, our co-founder and co-CEO, who splits his time between running the company alongside Pablo Viguera and staying close to what the team is building. That structure keeps decisions fast and puts PMs in direct conversation with the top of the company. Mexico's product and engineering team. A WEEK THAT TOUCHES EVERY PART OF THE BUSINESS Being a PM at Belvo means the job doesn't stop at product and engineering. Collaboration across teams is baked into the role, not an occasional ask, and for Kevin, that's one of the things that makes it interesting. "I don't see it as stepping outside my role. Sales, CS, engineering, they're all part of how a good product gets built here, so being close to them just makes me better at my job." - Kevin Nakabashi Customer success takes up just as much space: strategies to retain clients, gaps clients have noticed in the product, and pricing questions Kevin often resolves himself. "I go there, do some calculations for them, as I know the cost of the product, to see whether it makes sense or not," he says. Brazil's product and engineering team. Andrés, who is a product lead in Mexico, describes a similar rhythm split roughly into thirds: customer calls, working with engineers, and longer-term roadmap thinking. "I spend a lot of time with customers, and I really love it," he says. "That close contact gives me a very direct understanding of their needs and the problems we need to solve." When something in the product breaks, that balance shifts fast. "When something is down, the entire week becomes customer-facing," he says. Daniel, who focuses on Payments in Mexico, puts it simply: no two weeks look the same, and that's exactly what he likes about it. "From working with Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Ops, Legal, every day presents new challenges," he says. His days move constantly between the small details and the bigger bets, and he's found that leaning on AI tools helps him keep pace with the volume without losing depth on either end. STRATEGY, EXECUTION, AND THE REGULATOR Kevin's team builds Belvo's annual strategy each year, then breaks it into execution tracks with clear owners, running alongside new launches, maintenance, and regulatory obligations that don't pause for any of it. That last piece is bigger than most people expect. Kevin represents Belvo as a director at the Central Bank of Brazil (BACEN), signing and validating official reports on the company's behalf. The role extends to clients running on Belvo's infrastructure too: if a client faces a compliance issue tied to Belvo's rails, Belvo steps in to help resolve and report it alongside them. Recently, he has also been selected as the director of INIT (Brazilian Association of Payment Transaction Initiators), for the 2026 - 2028 term. The election comes shortly after Init secured a seat on Open Finance's governance council, the framework's definitive governance structure. For Daniel, what drew him to Belvo was the combination: a clear vision, a product with real depth, and a team he actually wanted to work with. In payments, most of what the team builds is about helping people get paid and pay, in a market where that's still often hard, expensive, or manual. "When we make a collection flow work better, or fix something so a charge shows up correctly on someone's bank statement, that's financial inclusion in a very concrete form," - Daniel Bañuelos THE HARDEST PART, AND THE BEST PART Ask Kevin what's hardest about the job, and the answer is scope: regulatory work, strategy, execution, clients, and sales all happening at once. What keeps him at Belvo three-plus years in is the other side of that same coin: real autonomy. "I set the pace I want, I have the autonomy I want," Kevin says. Belvo has a lean team , but a concentrated one, made up of people he considers sharp and thoughtful, which means the conversations stay substantive. And this is one of the things he values most about working here. New ideas get a real hearing, not a rubber stamp and not a dismissal. When something gets turned down, there's always a reason attached to it, and Kevin says the company is open to new ideas but mature enough to say "not right now" when that's the honest answer. Andrés' answer to the same question, the hardest part of the job, points somewhere similar: balancing the fires in front of him with the work that matters six months out. "The biggest challenge is balancing what's urgent today with what matters six months from now," he says. "In a market moving this fast, you have to keep supporting customers in the moment without losing sight of the bigger things you're building toward." Daniel points to a different kind of moment as the clearest example of the culture in action: a week-long war room. A small group met every day, worked through the data, built filters, ran cycles, and handled an incident in the middle of it all. What stuck with him wasn't the fix itself, it was how the team showed up: humble, direct, no finger-pointing, everyone owning their piece. "The bar was high and nobody flinched," he says. SIZE OF A SMALL COMPANY, STABILITY OF SOMETHING BIGGER Andrés joined Belvo after a career spanning early-stage startups and large global companies, and Belvo landed somewhere in between. He points to Belvo's documentation as stronger than what he saw at companies with a thousand or more employees, paired with a compensation and benefits structure that feels closer to a startup and a stability that doesn't. "Belvo feels big where it needs to feel big, but also small where it needs to feel small. We have strong processes and a huge amount of documentation, but at the same time it feels very horizontal. You can reach out to anyone, collaborate with anyone, and there's a lot of trust and ownership by default." - Andrés Alanís Andres at Belvolution, our annual company offsite. Ownership showed up early for him. Trust isn't something you earn slowly at Belvo, it's given upfront, and Andrés says he felt fully autonomous within three months of joining. That same posture, curiosity paired with humility, comes from the top. Andrés points to Pablo Viguera and Uri Tintoré as the ones modeling it, and says it shows up in how the whole team approaches problems. The recent wave of AI tools inside the company is one example: automations, internal chatbots, and small tools that people built on their own initiative. The curiosity was already there. AI just gave people a faster way to act on it. THE TAKEAWAY Product management at Belvo doesn't look like product management at a typical software company, and that's by design. For Kevin and Andrés, the wider scope is the point: more autonomy, more collaboration, and a seat in rooms most PMs elsewhere never get invited into. If that sounds like the kind of role you're looking for, check out our open positions.

body_text: View All News Citius Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Reports Fiscal Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update 08/14/2026 $7.1 Million in revenue for the first nine months of fiscal 2026 from commercial sales of LYMPHIR ® $17 million in cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, 2026 Expanded LYMPHIR commercial and medical affairs organizations deployed nationwide CRANFORD, N.J. , Aug. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Citius Pharmaceuticals, Inc. ("Citius Pharma" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: CTXR), a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the development and commercialization of first-in-class critical care products, today reported financial results for the fiscal third quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provided a business update, including progress at its majority-owned subsidiary, Citius Oncology, Inc. (Nasdaq: CTOR). "The LYMPHIR launch continued to build momentum in our fiscal third quarter and remains the primary driver of our business. The number of institutional vial orders increased, new institutions placed orders, and LYMPHIR became available at 44 leading academic oncology centers, NCCN institutions and community infusion centers. These indicators demonstrate meaningful progress in formulary access and treatment-driven demand as physicians gain familiarity with LYMPHIR's differentiated clinical profile," said Leonard Mazur, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Citius Pharma and Citius Oncology. "Following the quarter end, we completed the nationwide deployment of Citius Oncology's expanded commercial and medical affairs teams, which now total 29 professionals. These teams are positioned to leverage the existing platform established to support LYMPHIR's success, including patient hub services, marketing, reimbursement support, and market access. We believe our expanded organization will facilitate increased engagement with priority treatment centers, support formulary adoption and broaden access for eligible patients as the launch matures," added Mazur. "We also continued to advance LYMPHIR's longer-term value proposition. Phase 1 investigator-initiated data presented at ASCO demonstrated encouraging clinical activity and durable responses for LYMPHIR in combination with pembrolizumab in heavily pre-treated gynecologic malignancies. Additionally, Phase 1 data of LYMPHIR administered prior to CAR-T therapy in high-risk relapsed or refractory DLBCL, presented at the 2026 ASTCT® & CIBMTR® Tandem Meetings, showed an 86% objective response rate, including 57% complete response, with no dose-limiting toxicities observed. These positive signals point to LYMPHIR's potential beyond cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. As we scale, we remain focused on disciplined execution and building the long-term sustainable value of LYMPHIR," concluded Mazur. Fiscal Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights and Subsequent Developments Continued commercial momentum for LYMPHIR, with availability in 44 institutions, including academic oncology centers, leading National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) institutions and community infusion centers; Increased the number of new institutions ordering LYMPHIR by 80% and grew institutional vial orders from wholesalers by 31%; Drove continued institutional demand growth in July, with 383 vials ordered by institutions from wholesalers, the largest vial order month to date; Secured near universal payer coverage, with no reimbursement denials or preauthorization barriers reported to date; Expanded Citius Oncology's commercial organization by 21 commercial field-based professionals and added eight medical science liaisons, with nationwide deployment completed in August 2026 through EVERSANA, the Company's exclusive commercialization partner; Advanced Phase 1 investigator-initiated trials: Data were presented at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting evaluating LYMPHIR in combination with pembrolizumab in recurrent or refractory gynecologic malignancies: 24% overall response rate (ORR) and a 48% clinical benefit rate, and median progression-free survival of 20.5 months among patients achieving clinical benefit; Data were presented at the 2026 ASTCT® & CIBMTR® Tandem Meetings evaluating LYMPHIR administered prior to CAR-T therapy in high-risk relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL): 86% ORR, including 57% complete response (CR) and 29% partial response (PR), LYMPHIR was well-tolerated with no dose-limiting toxicities observed; Closed a registered direct offering in April 2026 for net proceeds of approximately $4.5 million; Received approximately $9.7 million in net proceeds from the exercise of certain warrants and funded $10.0 million under the first tranche of a Citius Oncology senior secured term loan facility of up to $25.0 million; and, Citius Oncology appointed Jonathan Peri, Ph.D., J.D., as an independent director, effective August 10, 2026, expanding the board to nine members. Fiscal Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights and Subsequent Developments Cash and cash equivalents of $17.0 million as of June 30, 2026; Revenues of $1.5 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with no revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2025; and $7.1 million for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, compared with no revenue for the nine months ended June 30, 2025; Gross profit of $1.0 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, representing a gross margin of approximately 67%, and $5.5 million for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, representing a gross margin of approximately 77%; Research and development expenses of $1.1 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $1.6 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025; and $4.3 million for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $7.5 million for the nine months ended June 30, 2025; General and administrative expenses of $6.1 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $4.4 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. General and administrative expenses were $38.3 million for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $14.6 million for the nine months ended June 30, 2025. The nine-month increase primarily reflects a non-recurring $19.7 million contract cancellation charge recognized in March 2026 and increased expenses related to the commercial launch of LYMPHIR; Stock-based compensation expense of $3.8 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $2.7 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025; and $11.9 million for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $7.9 million for the nine months ended June 30, 2025; and, Net loss applicable to common stockholders of $8.9 million, or $(0.34) per share, for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $8.8 million, or $(0.80) per share, for the three months ended June 30, 2025; and $38.3 million, or $(1.64) per share, for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $29.5 million, or $(3.27) per share, for the nine months ended June 30, 2025. body_text: Revenue reaches quarterly record as Precipio returns to positive Adjusted EBITDA and strengthens cash position NEW HAVEN, CT, Globenewswire – (Aug 14, 2026) – Specialty cancer diagnostics company Precipio, Inc. (NASDAQ: PRPO) , announces financial results for the second quarter that ended June 30, 2026. Below are some of the key financial performance metrics for the Company. For additional results please see the Company’s Form 10-Q which was filed today. Revenue – $7.0M vs. $6.7M in Q1-2026, and up 22% YoY from $5.7M in Q2-2025. This comprised of $6.1M in pathology revenue (up from $6.0M in Q1) and $0.9M in product revenue (up from $0.66M in Q1). Adjusted EBITDA – $0.4M vs. $(0.2)M in Q1-2026. The change was driven by increased revenues of $0.3 million and a decrease in stock-based compensation expense of $0.2M. Cash flow – Cash Flow generated from operations was $0.7M in Q2-2026; total increase in cash was $0.5 million, resulting in an end of quarter cash balance exceeding $3M, vs $1.1M in Q2-2025. “As anticipated, Q2 operating performance reflects a healthy recovery and continued momentum across the business, with customer growth generating quarterly revenue surpassing $7M for the first time in Company history. Product revenues increased 21% from the previous high of $750K in Q4-2025, and cash increased to over $3M.” said Ilan Danieli, CEO of Precipio. “We’ve achieved this level of cash without a financing event, demonstrating the strength of our operations. We’re encouraged by the progress we’ve made and believe we are well positioned to continue building on this momentum.” Additional information and a more in-depth discussion on the Company’s Q2-2026 performance will be provided in the shareholder call on August 17th, 2026, at 5 PM ET. The call will include remarks by management on the Company’s core business, followed by a moderated Q&A session. EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Reconciliation and Explanation EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) is a non-GAAP financial measure that is widely used to evaluate operational performance and pre-tax profitability of emerging growth companies like ours. Management believes Adjusted EBITDA provides investors with a useful perspective on the Company’s financial health, particularly where non-cash amortization has an important impact on profitability. Adjusted EBITDA as we define it modifies EBITDA by excluding the non-cash costs of employee stock options and unusual non-operating income and expense. Our mission is to address the pervasive problem of cancer misdiagnoses by developing solutions in the form of diagnostic products and services. Our products and services deliver higher accuracy, improved laboratory workflow, and ultimately better patient outcomes, which reduce healthcare expenses. Precipio develops innovative technologies in our laboratory where we design, test, validate, and use these products clinically, improving diagnostic outcomes. Precipio then commercializes these technologies as proprietary products that serve the global laboratory community and further scales Precipio’s reach to eradicate misdiagnosis. title: Genasys Reaches Major Milestone – Over 50M U.S. Residents Covered by Protect Platform
summary: Over 50M U.S. residents covered by Genasys Protect zone-based public safety communication and emergency alerting coverage
body_text: Company’s Zone-Based Public Safety Communication and Emergency Alerting Coverage Now Extends to 20% of U.S. by Area SAN DIEGO, CA – August 10, 2026 – Genasys Inc. (NASDAQ: GNSS), the global leader in Protective Communications ®, today announced that its Protect software platform, which includes Genasys Protect ® and Genasys Evertel ® (Evertel), now covers 15% of the U.S. population and 20% of the country by area, making it the nation’s leading platform for zone-based emergency alerting, evacuation management, and secure, real-time communication. “Covering more than 50 million people is an important milestone that reflects the growing trust communities and public safety agencies place in Genasys life safety solutions,” said Richard Danforth, CEO of Genasys Inc. “Last summer’s deadly flooding in Texas and several recent tragedies illustrate the ineffectiveness of single channel, general warnings. Genasys Protect delivers multi-channel emergency notifications up to 90% faster than other warning systems using data-driven decisions, precise zone targeting, and clear messaging.” Whether it’s a neighborhood evacuation order for a natural gas leak, an active SWAT operation shelter-in-place advisory for a few city blocks, or a severe weather alert for a county or community, Genasys Protect’s zone-based alerting helps ensure only the people in affected areas receive emergency notifications. Zone-based alerting provides vital advantages during wildfires, flooding, hazardous material incidents, and other public safety threats. By delivering the right message to the right people at the right time, Genasys Protect reduces alert fatigue, builds public trust, and enhances overall incident response. In addition to Genasys Protect, Evertel has grown to support mission-critical communications for more than 500 law enforcement agencies in 45 states. Since its acquisition by Genasys less than three years ago, Evertel has doubled its customer base and is now deployed in some of the largest U.S. cities. “When it comes to encrypted, legally compliant mission-critical communications, we provide agencies access to any other public safety agency with complete security, transparency, and government accountability,” said Chief Jeff Halstead (Ret.), Genasys Director of Strategic Accounts and Evertel Founder. Evertel is a FOIA, CJIS, HIPAA, and State compliant communications and team collaboration platform for first responders and government agencies. Evertel greatly enhances communications with voice, chat, messaging, video, and images, empowering teams to share critical information and receive agency-wide and cross-agency updates in a secure, real-time environment. About Genasys Inc. Genasys is the global leader in Protective Communications®, providing the most comprehensive portfolio of preparedness, response, and analytics software and hardware solutions available. The company’s Long Range Acoustic Device® (LRAD®) and Protect Platform, which includes Genasys Protect® and Genasys Evertel®, are designed around one premise: ensuring organizations and public safety agencies are Ready when it matters ®. Protecting people and saving lives for over 40 years, Genasys covers more than 155 million people in all 50 states and in over 100 countries worldwide. For more information, visit genasys.com . title: Cómo hacer una nómina en Colombia paso a paso
summary: Hacer una nómina en Colombia consiste en calcular, para cada trabajador y cada periodo de pago, el total devengado (salario, auxilio de transporte, horas extra).
body_text: Hacer una nómina en Colombia consiste en calcular, para cada trabajador y cada periodo de pago, el total devengado (salario, auxilio de transporte, horas extra), restarle las deducciones legales (salud, pensión, retención en la fuente), sumar los aportes patronales a seguridad social y parafiscales, provisionar las prestaciones sociales y, finalmente, expedir el comprobante de nómina electrónica ante la DIAN. Esta guía explica cada paso con las cifras vigentes de 2026 y un ejemplo completo de liquidación. ¿Qué es la nómina y qué conceptos incluye? La nómina es el proceso periódico —mensual, quincenal o semanal— mediante el cual una empresa calcula y paga a sus trabajadores el salario y demás conceptos derivados de la relación laboral, y liquida ante el sistema de seguridad social los aportes que le corresponden como empleador. No se trata solo del pago que recibe el trabajador: también incluye los aportes que la empresa asume adicionalmente y las provisiones de prestaciones sociales que se pagan en momentos distintos del año, como la prima o las cesantías. El periodo de liquidación no puede superar el mes calendario, aunque el pago efectivo al trabajador puede ser quincenal o semanal. Reúne la información base de cada trabajador Antes de calcular cualquier valor, es indispensable tener consolidada la siguiente información de cada empleado: Tipo de contrato (término fijo, indefinido, obra o labor, aprendizaje) y fecha de ingreso. Salario base pactado y si es ordinario o salario integral. Si el trabajador tiene derecho a auxilio de transporte (ingresos hasta 2 SMMLV y necesidad de desplazamiento). Novedades del periodo: incapacidades, licencias, vacaciones, horas extra, recargos nocturnos o dominicales, comisiones. Deducciones autorizadas: libranzas, embargos judiciales, aportes voluntarios a pensión o AFC. Fondo de pensiones, EPS y caja de compensación a la que está afiliado. Número de dependientes económicos, si aplica, para efectos de retención en la fuente. Calcula el total devengado del periodo El devengado es la suma de todo lo que el trabajador tiene derecho a recibir en el periodo: salario ordinario, auxilio de transporte (si aplica), horas extra, recargos nocturnos o dominicales, comisiones y cualquier bonificación de carácter salarial. Con las cifras de 2026, un trabajador con salario mínimo que recibe auxilio de transporte tiene un devengado mensual de: $1.750.905 (salario) + $249.095 (auxilio de transporte) = $2.000.000 Es importante recordar que el auxilio de transporte no hace parte del Ingreso Base de Cotización (IBC) para seguridad social, pero sí se incluye en la base para liquidar las prestaciones sociales. Aplica las deducciones legales del trabajador Sobre el IBC (el salario sin auxilio de transporte) se descuentan los aportes obligatorios que le corresponden al trabajador, además de la retención en la fuente cuando el ingreso lo amerita y otras deducciones autorizadas: Concepto Porcentaje o base Valor con SMMLV 2026 ($1.750.905) Aporte a salud (trabajador) 4% del IBC $70.036 Aporte a pensión (trabajador) 4% del IBC $70.036 Retención en la fuente Según tabla de retención DIAN (aplica desde ingresos más altos) $0 para SMMLV Fondo de solidaridad pensional Solo si el IBC es igual o superior a 4 SMMLV No aplica Total deducciones (ejemplo SMMLV) $140.072 Con esas deducciones, el neto a pagar del ejemplo sería: $2.000.000 (devengado) − $140.072 (deducciones) = $1.859.928 . Calcula los aportes patronales a seguridad social y parafiscales Además de lo que se descuenta al trabajador, el empleador debe asumir aportes adicionales sobre el mismo IBC. Muchas empresas que son contribuyentes del impuesto de renta y tienen trabajadores que devengan individualmente menos de 10 SMMLV están exoneradas del pago de salud, SENA e ICBF, gracias al beneficio vigente desde la Ley 1819 de 2016: Concepto Tarifa ¿Aplica exoneración? Salud (empleador) 8,5% del IBC Exonerado si cumple los requisitos de ley Pensión (empleador) 12% del IBC No exonerable, siempre se paga ARL (riesgos laborales) Entre 0,522% y 6,96% del IBC, según clase de riesgo No exonerable SENA 2% del IBC Exonerado si cumple los requisitos de ley ICBF 3% del IBC Exonerado si cumple los requisitos de ley Caja de Compensación Familiar 4% del IBC No exonerable, siempre se paga Para una empresa exonerada con un trabajador de salario mínimo (riesgo laboral clase I, 0,522%), el aporte patronal mensual sería aproximadamente: pensión $210.109 + ARL $9.140 + caja de compensación $70.036 = cerca de $289.285 . Provisiona las prestaciones sociales Las prestaciones sociales no se descuentan del trabajador ni se pagan cada mes en efectivo, pero deben provisionarse mensualmente en la contabilidad porque se liquidan y pagan en fechas específicas del año: Prestación Porcentaje o fórmula Momento de pago Cesantías 8,33% del salario mensual (equivalente a 1 salario por año) Antes del 14 de febrero, al Fondo de Cesantías Intereses sobre cesantías 12% anual sobre el saldo de cesantías Antes del 31 de enero, directamente al trabajador Prima de servicios 8,33% del salario mensual (equivalente a 1 salario por año) 30 de junio y 20 de diciembre Vacaciones 4,17% del salario mensual (15 días hábiles por año) Al momento de disfrutarlas o liquidarlas Para el ejemplo del salario mínimo con auxilio de transporte, la provisión mensual de prestaciones sociales asciende aproximadamente a $426.000, lo que equivale a cerca del 21,83% del devengado, porcentaje que suele usarse como referencia rápida para estimar el costo prestacional total. Ejemplo práctico completo: liquidación con salario mínimo 2026 Reuniendo todos los pasos anteriores, así queda el costo total mensual para la empresa por un trabajador con salario mínimo, auxilio de transporte y beneficio de exoneración de aportes: Devengado del trabajador: $2.000.000 Deducciones del trabajador (salud + pensión): $140.072 Neto que recibe el trabajador: $1.859.928 Aportes patronales a seguridad social y parafiscales: $289.285 Provisión de prestaciones sociales: $426.000 Costo total mensual para la empresa: cerca de $2.715.000 Este último valor —y no el salario nominal— es el que realmente debe presupuestar una empresa al planear la contratación de personal, y explica por qué el costo de un trabajador siempre es superior a lo que recibe en su cuenta. Genera y valida el comprobante de nómina electrónica Desde la implementación de la nómina electrónica, todo empleador con trabajadores dependientes debe generar un documento soporte de nómina electrónica y transmitirlo a la DIAN por cada periodo liquidado. Este comprobante debe incluir, entre otros datos: Identificación del trabajador y del empleador. Periodo liquidado y días trabajados. Todos los conceptos devengados, desagregados por tipo (salario, auxilio de transporte, horas extra, comisiones). Deducciones aplicadas y su detalle. Aportes a seguridad social del periodo. Neto pagado al trabajador. Omitir o transmitir de forma incorrecta la nómina electrónica no solo genera riesgo de sanción, sino que puede implicar la pérdida de deducibilidad fiscal de esos costos laborales en la declaración de renta de la empresa. Paga los aportes a través de la PILA Una vez cerrada la nómina, el empleador debe consolidar y pagar los aportes a seguridad social (salud, pensión, ARL) y parafiscales (SENA, ICBF, caja de compensación) mediante la Planilla Integrada de Liquidación de Aportes (PILA), a través de un operador autorizado. El plazo de pago varía según el último dígito del NIT del empleador y generalmente se ubica entre el día 1 y el día 20 del mes siguiente al periodo liquidado. Aunque el pago al trabajador sea quincenal o semanal, la PILA siempre se liquida y paga de forma mensual. Errores comunes al elaborar la nómina Incluir el auxilio de transporte dentro del IBC para calcular seguridad social, cuando no debe hacer parte de esa base. Calcular las vacaciones incluyendo el auxilio de transporte, que tampoco integra esa base. Aplicar la exoneración de parafiscales sin verificar que la empresa cumple realmente los requisitos legales para acceder a ella. Confundir el neto mensual del trabajador con el total de sus prestaciones sociales, que se pagan en fechas distintas del año. No actualizar el valor de la hora ordinaria cuando cambia la jornada máxima legal, lo que afecta el cálculo de horas extra y recargos. No transmitir a tiempo el documento soporte de nómina electrónica ante la DIAN. Herramientas y buenas prácticas para simplificar la nómina Llevar la nómina en hojas de cálculo es viable para empresas muy pequeñas, pero a medida que crece el número de trabajadores aumenta el riesgo de errores en fórmulas, novedades y plazos. Un software de nómina especializado ayuda a automatizar el cálculo de deducciones, aportes y prestaciones, generar la nómina electrónica en el formato que exige la DIAN, controlar vencimientos de PILA y mantener un histórico auditable de cada liquidación, lo que resulta especialmente valioso cuando el equipo contable debe responder ante una auditoría o una inspección del Ministerio del Trabajo. Preguntas frecuentes sobre cómo hacer la nómina en Colombia ¿Con qué periodicidad se puede pagar la nómina? El pago al trabajador puede ser semanal, quincenal o mensual, pero el periodo máximo para liquidar conceptos como seguridad social y parafiscales ante la PILA siempre es mensual. ¿Todas las empresas tienen derecho a la exoneración de parafiscales? No. La exoneración de salud, SENA e ICBF aplica a personas jurídicas contribuyentes del impuesto de renta y a personas naturales empleadoras que cumplen ciertos requisitos, siempre que cada trabajador devengue individualmente menos de 10 SMMLV. La pensión, el ARL y la caja de compensación nunca se exoneran. ¿Qué pasa si un trabajador tiene incapacidad durante el mes? Los primeros dos días de incapacidad de origen común los asume el empleador al 66,67% del salario; a partir del tercer día, ese porcentaje lo reconoce la EPS, aunque el empleador suele pagarlo primero y luego solicitar el reembolso. ¿Es obligatoria la nómina electrónica para todas las empresas, sin importar el tamaño? Sí, todo empleador con trabajadores vinculados por contrato de trabajo debe generar y transmitir el documento soporte de nómina electrónica a la DIAN, independientemente de su tamaño o régimen tributario. Hacer una nómina en Colombia va más allá de calcular el salario neto de cada trabajador: implica sumar devengados, aplicar deducciones legales, calcular aportes patronales, provisionar prestaciones sociales y cumplir con la nómina electrónica y la PILA dentro de los plazos establecidos. Seguir este proceso de forma ordenada, con las cifras actualizadas cada año, reduce errores, evita contingencias laborales y fiscales, y permite a la empresa conocer con precisión el verdadero costo de su nómina.

title: DIY investing vs robo-advisors: Which is better?
summary: Robo-advisors aren't actually robots. A registered human is responsible for your portfolio, and that changes how you should compare your options. The fee gap looks tiny on paper. See what half a percent actually costs you on a $100,000 portfolio. There's a third option most comparisons skip, and it keeps both the low fees and the autopilot.
body_text: Highlights: Robo-advisors aren't actually robots. A registered human is responsible for your portfolio, and that changes how you should compare your options. The fee gap looks tiny on paper. See what half a percent actually costs you on a $100,000 portfolio. There's a third option most comparisons skip, and it keeps both the low fees and the autopilot. If you've decided to start investing without an advisor, you've probably hit this fork in the road: hand it to a robo-advisor, or do it yourself? Here's a clear look at both options, what they cost, and a third option that sits between them. Quick answer: DIY investing or a robo-advisor? Both options have their positives and negatives. A robo-advisor is better if you want to be completely hands-off and don't mind paying a yearly fee for that. DIY is better if you want the lowest cost and full control, and you're willing to do a little recurring upkeep. The cost difference is the big lever. Robo-advisors in Canada typically run about 0.5% to 1% of your balance per year all-in. DIY costs only what your ETFs charge, which is a small fraction of that. There's also a middle path: manage your own portfolio and use a tool to automate the tedious parts. More on that below. What a robo-advisor actually does A robo-advisor is a service that builds and manages a portfolio for you. You answer a questionnaire about your goals, timeline, and how much risk you feel comfortable with. The service puts your money into a ready-made mix of low-cost ETFs and keeps it balanced over time. Despite the name, a robo-advisor is not just a robot making decisions on its own. For example, in Ontario, online investment advisers provide discretionary portfolio management, and a human adviser is involved in and responsible for the investment decisions made for you. The idea is simple: you deposit money, they handle everything else. Rebalancing, reinvesting, staying the course when markets wobble. You never have to place a trade or know what a ticker symbol is. The tradeoff is control and cost. You get their model portfolio, not yours. And you pay a management fee every year, forever, on your whole balance. What DIY investing actually involves DIY investing means opening an account at a brokerage like Wealthsimple or Questrade, picking your own investments, and managing them yourself. For most people following a passive strategy, that means choosing a few index ETFs , deciding on a mix, and buying regularly. The good news: it's cheaper than any managed option, and you're in full control. The tradeoff is that you do the work. Every deposit, you figure out what to buy. When your mix drifts away from your target, you notice it (or you don't), do the math, and place the trades. You keep yourself calm in a downturn with nobody on the other end of the phone. None of this is hard math. It's just recurring, slightly tedious, and easy to put off. DIY portfolios can drift because nobody got around to rebalancing. What each one costs This is where the comparison gets real. According to MoneySense's 2026 robo-advisor guide , robo-advisors in Canada typically cost about 0.5% to 1% of your money per year once you include both the management fee and the fees inside the ETFs they use. Half a percent sounds like pocket change. On a $100,000 portfolio, 0.75% is $750 a year. Every year. And the dollar amount grows as your portfolio grows, even though the work of managing it doesn't. Stretch that over 20 years and the pocket change becomes real money. At a 7% annual return, $100,000 grows to about $387,000 before fees. But with a 0.75% annual fee, you’d end up with roughly $337,000 instead. That’s about $50,000 less, because every dollar paid in fees is a dollar that no longer gets to compound. DIY costs much less. You still pay each ETF's own built-in management fee, which for broad index ETFs is typically a small fraction of a percent, plus whatever your brokerage charges per trade (many now charge nothing for ETF purchases). There's no management fee on top, because you're the manager. Over decades, that gap compounds. The question is whether the savings are worth your time and attention. So which is better? It depends on which of these sounds more like you. A robo-advisor probably fits if: you want to be completely hands-off, you'd rather pay a fee than think about your portfolio, or you know yourself well enough to know you'd never actually get around to rebalancing. DIY probably fits if: you want the lowest possible cost, you like having full control over what you own, and you're willing to do a bit of recurring upkeep to keep your plan on track. Neither answer is wrong. A robo-advisor that keeps you invested beats a DIY plan you abandon. A DIY plan you actually follow beats paying a fee for something you could do yourself. Here's how the three approaches compare at a glance: The middle path: DIY with the boring parts handled Here's the thing most comparisons miss. The ‘work’ of a DIY portfolio can be automated, so you keep control and don’t have to pay a percentage of your portfolio. That's where a tool like Passiv sits in. You use your own brokerage account, your own ETFs, and your own target mix. Passiv watches it for you, tells you when new cash arrives, and does the math on what to buy to stay on target. You place the trades, so nothing happens without you. You get some of the convenience people like about robo-advisors, while keeping the control and lower fee structure of DIY investing. No percentage fee scaling up with your balance, just your ETFs' own small built-in fees. Make it even easier with Passiv Elite The free version tells you what to buy, and you go place those trades at your brokerage. Passiv Elite removes that last step too. With one-click trades, Elite turns the whole chore into a single button. New cash lands, Passiv does the math, and one click places all your trades so your portfolio will stay balanced. You get the ease of a robo-advisor, while staying in control of your investments. Frequently asked questions Do robo-advisors get better returns than DIY investing? Not inherently. Both typically hold similar low-cost index ETFs, so they ride the same markets. The difference in outcomes usually comes down to two things: fees, where DIY wins, and behaviour, where whichever approach keeps you invested and on-plan wins. Can I switch from a robo-advisor to DIY later? Yes. You can transfer your account to a self-directed brokerage. Ask for a direct transfer rather than cashing out, since selling investments in a non-registered account can trigger tax on any gains. Your old institution may charge a transfer-out fee, and some brokerages periodically offer to cover it, but terms change, so check before acting. Is DIY investing safe for a beginner? The mechanics are simpler than they used to be. An all-in-one ETF gives you a diversified portfolio in a single purchase. The bigger risk for beginners typically isn't picking wrong, it's behaviour: panic selling, chasing trends, or abandoning the plan. If you're not confident you'll stay the course alone, that's a fair reason to start with a robo-advisor. Do I need a lot of money to start either way? No. Most robo-advisors have low or no minimums, and DIY can start with a single ETF purchase. What matters more than the starting amount is contributing regularly. What's the cheapest way to invest in Canada? DIY with broad index ETFs, since you skip the management fee entirely. The tradeoff is that you're responsible for the upkeep, which is exactly the gap free tools can fill. Want to make DIY investing easy? Passiv's Forever Free account does the math for you, tells you when your portfolio has drifted, and tracks everything across your accounts, all without paying a cent. Set up your target portfolio in about 10 minutes.

HitPay vs Airwallex Philippines: Which Is Better for SMEs?

body_text: Quick Answer: For Philippine SMEs that need to accept GCash, Maya, QR Ph, InstaPay, PESONet, and over-the-counter payments with no monthly fees and next business day payouts in PHP, HitPay is the stronger fit. Airwallex is licensed and operational in the Philippines but is positioned primarily as a global treasury and FX platform rather than a local payment acceptance solution. HitPay supports 50+ payment methods across Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines, with free sign-up and approval in 1–3 business days. Philippine e-commerce and retail are growing rapidly, with digital payments now central to how consumers in Makati, BGC, Cebu, and Davao pay for goods and services. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) has set a target for at least 50% of retail payments to be done digitally — a policy direction that has accelerated merchant adoption of QR Ph, GCash, and InstaPay. Choosing the right payment gateway shapes cash flow timing, checkout conversion, and operational overhead from day one. What payment methods do HitPay and Airwallex support in the Philippines? This is where the two platforms diverge most sharply for local merchants. HitPay supports the full stack of Philippine payment methods: GCash, Maya, QR Ph, ShopeePay, SPayLater, GrabPay, BillEase, UnionBank Online, InstaPay, PESONet, Visa, Mastercard, and over-the-counter options via Bayad, ECPay, and Palawan. Merchants running a boutique in BGC or a food business in Quezon City can accept payments from virtually every customer segment — banked, underbanked, and those who pay via convenience stores. HitPay also enables cross-border e-wallet acceptance, so Philippine merchants can receive payments from international visitors using PayNow (Singapore), QRIS (Indonesia), PromptPay (Thailand), TrueMoney (Thailand), LINE Pay (Thailand), DuitNow (Malaysia), and KakaoPay, PayCo, and LINE Pay (South Korea). Cross-border method activation takes 3–5 business days after submission. Airwallex’s Philippines offering centres on global card acceptance and multi-currency accounts. Its checkout product supports cards and select wallets globally, but its local Philippine e-wallet coverage — GCash, Maya, QR Ph — is not a published core feature of its merchant acceptance product. Airwallex’s strength is in FX transfers, multi-currency corporate cards, and treasury management for businesses with cross-border payment flows. For Philippine merchants evaluating ecommerce payment solutions for Southeast Asia , the absence of monthly fees is often the deciding factor at early and growth stages. What are the payout timelines for Philippine merchants? HitPay settles domestic PHP transactions on the next business day. Cross-border transactions (e.g. a Singapore customer paying via PayNow at a Manila merchant’s checkout) settle at T+2. This predictable cash flow timeline is significant for SMEs managing inventory or supplier payments. Airwallex offers multi-currency account holding and global payouts, which can be valuable for businesses with overseas suppliers or international revenue. However, its settlement timeline for domestic PHP merchant transactions is not published with the same specificity. Businesses that primarily collect from local Filipino customers benefit more from a gateway with transparent, fast domestic settlement. HitPay’s payment gateway for the Philippines is built around next business day PHP payouts as a baseline, not a premium feature. Which platform is better for Philippine SME operations? Xendit and Fiuu are two other gateways Philippine merchants evaluate — both with local e-wallet support — but the comparison between HitPay and Airwallex is most telling because the platforms serve fundamentally different use cases. Airwallex is built for businesses managing treasury across multiple currencies, paying overseas suppliers, or issuing multi-currency corporate cards to a distributed team. It is a financial operations platform first and a payment acceptance tool second. HitPay is built for merchants who need to accept money from Filipino customers — online, in-person, or via payment links — across the widest possible set of local methods. It is PCI DSS compliant, MAS-licensed (PS20200643), and registered with the BSP as an Operator of Payment System. Free to sign up, with approval in 1–3 business days. For accepting GCash and QR Ph payments at a brick-and-mortar store , HitPay’s Scan to Pay feature allows merchants to generate a QR code from the mobile app and accept payments instantly — no additional hardware required. Best for: HitPay Philippine SMEs — retail, food and beverage, online stores, service businesses — that want zero monthly fees, 50+ payment methods including GCash, Maya, QR Ph, InstaPay, PESONet, and over-the-counter channels, with next business day PHP payouts and no setup cost. Best for: Airwallex Businesses with significant cross-border treasury needs, overseas supplier payments, or multi-currency expense management requirements — where global FX efficiency matters more than breadth of local Philippine e-wallet acceptance. Frequently Asked Questions Does Airwallex support GCash and QR Ph for Philippine merchants? Airwallex's Philippines merchant acceptance product does not list GCash, Maya, or QR Ph as published core features. HitPay supports all three, along with ShopeePay, GrabPay, BillEase, InstaPay, PESONet, and over-the-counter channels, making it the stronger choice for merchants whose customers use local Philippine payment methods. Does HitPay charge a monthly fee in the Philippines? HitPay charges no monthly fee and no setup fee in the Philippines. Merchants pay only per transaction. Check Airwallex's pricing page directly for their current plan costs, as these may change over time. How fast does HitPay pay out PHP to Philippine merchants? HitPay settles domestic PHP transactions on the next business day. Cross-border transactions — for example, a Singapore customer paying via PayNow at a Philippine merchant's checkout — settle at T+2. This applies to all Philippine merchants on HitPay with no minimum volume requirement. Is HitPay licensed to operate in the Philippines? Yes. HitPay is Singapore-headquartered and licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (licence PS20200643). In the Philippines, HitPay Payment Solutions Inc is registered with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) as an Operator of Payment System (OPSCOR-2023-0006) and is also registered with the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC). For a small online store in Manila, is HitPay or Airwallex the better choice? For a small online store in Manila accepting payments from Filipino customers, HitPay is the more practical choice. It supports GCash, Maya, QR Ph, cards, and InstaPay out of the box with no monthly fees and next business day payouts in PHP. Airwallex is better suited to businesses with cross-border treasury or multi-currency expense management needs rather than local Philippine consumer payment acceptance. How long does it take to get approved on HitPay in the Philippines? HitPay approves new merchant accounts in 1–3 business days. Sign-up is free with no setup fee.
